parsed.study_design: Qualitative institutional case study using field investigations, documentary analysis, and administrative statistics
parsed.population_and_sample: Rural and semi-urban communities, water users, Water Users Associations, municipalities, public agencies, NGOs, and public/private water-service operators; no numerical fieldwork sample is reported.
parsed.exposure: The 2000 rural and semi-urban water-sector reform, decentralization and transfer of responsibilities to municipalities, creation/restructuring of Water Users Associations, delegated management, participation requirements, and water-tariff rules.
parsed.outcome: Drinking-water access and coverage, infrastructure functionality and service continuity, affordability and payment arrangements, territorial disparities, exclusion of women and migrants, and the effectiveness of local service governance.
parsed.rationale: The article analyzes how institutional reforms and Water Users Associations affect drinking-water access in rural and semi-urban Burkina Faso, drawing on field studies identified in the opening note and on documentary and administrative evidence. Sections 2.1–2.4 report access rates, infrastructure functionality, tariff and payment practices, exclusion mechanisms, and field-observed implementation gaps, including that only 63.6% of AUEs were functional (p. 545). Although the methods and sample are only sparsely described, the population, governance exposures, access outcomes, and qualitative institutional case-study design are sufficiently identifiable; French translation is feasible.
